{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-co-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"cb24122130dad93c39e0cd59438a4de291c81035cf6c92ea8429d1b5abcf957b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-co-class-std:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"bdc8d5a61f622fc6c91da0be8478dfb02615c007374129c91888edf82eb1b746","source_liveness_sha256":"1b8565daf88dec5a1936ad41ec3e529347f3ec6b06db1d191293e01d45d7ee05"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Railroad crossings, light rail and bicyclists","heading":"C2 — Confusables and KG hints: railroad crossings, light rail and bicyclists","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusables and KG hints: railroad crossings, light rail and bicyclists

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
A crossbuck is a yield-type sign that becomes regulatory as a train approaches, while flashing lights and lowered gates always mean stop. [A01]
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty three; confusable sec13-F11 vs sec13-F13 vs sec13-F14. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
The round advance warning sign only tells you a crossing is ahead in time to stop, while the crossbuck carries a yield duty. [A01]
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty two; confusable sec13-F08 vs sec13-F11. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
With no stop line painted, keep at least 10 feet from the rails, because a train overhangs the tracks by 3 feet. [A01]
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty two; prereq sec13-F09. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
A train looks slower than it is, and a freight train at 55 mph needs about a mile to stop, so judge its speed and distance carefully. [A01]
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty two; prereq sec13-F07. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A01
A stalled car on the tracks calls for getting everyone out and away first and phoning the ENS number or police second. [A01]
Why it matters: group railroad; difficulty two; prereq sec13-F06 and sec13-F16. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A02
The three-foot bicyclist gap allows briefly crossing a double yellow line when nothing is oncoming; if three feet is impossible, stay behind the rider. [A02]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty three; prereq sec13-F28 and sec13-F29. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A02
A bicyclist in the center of the lane or riding side by side may be within the law, for visibility or hazard avoidance, as long as normal traffic is not impeded. [A02]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty two; confusable sec13-F27 vs sec13-F30. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A02
Whether bicyclists may ride on sidewalks depends on local ordinance, not one statewide rule. [A02]
Why it matters: group bicyclists; difficulty two; prereq sec13-F25. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0025]

Misconception: you may drive around a light rail gate once the train has passed; another may come from the opposite direction. [A02]
Misconception: quiet-zone crossings give no warning; the flashing lights and gates still warn you. [A01]
Misconception: a bike lane ends at the intersection where its paint stops; it continues through. [A02]
Misconception: a hanging overhead wire is safe if it is not sparking; assume it is live and never touch it. [A02]
Mnemonic: Round sign means railroad ahead. [A01]
Mnemonic: Look back before the door opens, reach across to open it. [A02]
Glossary: Crossbuck means the railroad crossing sign treated like a yield sign. [A01]
Glossary: Quiet zone means a crossing where train horns do not sound, marked by a No Train Horn sign. [A01]
Glossary: Catenary means the overhead wire system above light rail tracks, always to be treated as electrified. [A02]
Glossary: Door zone means the strip beside parked cars that bicyclists may avoid by riding in the center of the lane. [A02]
